--- Item 2 ---
id: fig_outcomes
figure_type: data
title: Outcome distributions
caption: >-
  Distribution of the primary outcome, rarefied field breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m=50$), over the 7,203 of 12,499 frame concepts
  that have at least 50 papers in the $t_0{+}6$..$t_0{+}8$ outcome window ($O_{2r}$ is undefined below that). (a) Histogram
  of $O_{2r}$ in 1-field bins centred on the integers. The dashed orange line marks the median (4.73) and the light-blue band
  the interquartile range [3.41, 6.20]. The distribution is mildly right-skewed: most concepts reach 2--8 fields and a thin
  tail extends to 14. (b) $O_{2r}$ against the raw field count, the number of venue fields holding at least 15 of the concept's
  outcome-window papers. Grey dots are concepts (x jittered), blue diamonds are per-count medians (counts with $n \geq 5$)
  and the dashed black line is the 1:1 line. Rarefied breadth lies above the 1:1 line for 97.6\% of concepts and rises only
  weakly with the raw count (Spearman $\rho = 0.31$). It is nearly independent of outcome-window volume ($\rho = -0.06$),
  whereas the thresholded raw count grows with volume ($\rho = 0.41$). Rarefaction thus separates size-adjusted breadth from
  volume-driven field counts.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-
  Main panel: histogram of rarefied field breadth O2r (m=50) for 12,499 concepts. X-axis: 'Rarefied field breadth (O2r, m=50)'
  ranging from 1.0 to 12.0. Y-axis: 'Number of concepts' ranging from 0 to 2500. The distribution is right-skewed with a peak
  around 2.0-2.5, median marked with a dashed red vertical line at 2.8, IQR shaded in light blue from 1.6 to 4.9. Bins are
  0.5 wide. Most mass is between 1.0 and 5.0, with a long tail to 12. Inset panel (top-right corner, about 40% width): scatterplot
  of rarefied breadth (y-axis, 1-12) versus raw field count (x-axis, 1-20). Points are semi-transparent gray dots showing
  a positive but noisy relationship. A diagonal reference line shows the 1:1 mapping if breadth equalled field count. Points
  scatter well below the line for high field counts, showing that rarefaction separates breadth from raw count. White background,
  black axis labels, sans-serif font, grid lines in light gray.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'
summary: >-
  Distribution of the primary outcome measure showing the right-skewed spread of rarefied breadth and its distinction from
  raw field counts.
figure_path: figures/fig_outcomes_v0.pdf

--- Item 4 ---
id: fig_full_screen
figure_type: data
title: Complete indicator screen
caption: >-
  Complete indicator screen for rarefied cross-field breadth (O2r). (a) Partial Spearman $\rho$ (PSP, controlling for rank(B5)
  plus group and onset-year dummies) of all 53 screened indicators on the DEV fields (CS, Engineering, BGM, Medicine), one
  row per family. Colour marks the family: retained frontier (FR), co-occurrence ego network (A), gateway landing (G), disciplinary
  spread (F), popularity (E) and co-author reach (S). Large filled circles are the 7 indicators confirmed on held-out fields;
  large open circles are the 3 selected on DEV but not confirmed; small dots are the 43 not selected. Selection kept indicators
  whose DEV 95\% CI excluded zero with at most 30\% missing, ranked them by $|$PSP$|$ and dropped near-duplicates ($|\rho|>0.85$).
  This is why some high-ranking DEV indicators (e.g.\ D\_rca\_end, and D\_rare, 88\% missing) are small dots. (b) The frozen
  top 10 in DEV rank order. Grey squares are the DEV estimates with 95\% concept-bootstrap CIs. Circles are held-out estimates
  pooled by DerSimonian--Laird over the PHYS, LIFEENV, SOC and MATHDEC groups, with 95\% CIs. Filled circles are confirmed
  (Holm $p<0.05$ with the frozen sign). All four retained-frontier (FR) and all three co-occurrence (A) selections replicate
  out of field. The gateway (G) and disciplinary-spread (F) selections shrink towards zero and are not confirmed. The held-out
  outcomes had been read once before by an earlier experiment. About half of the M0\_density\_end and D\_vol\_end effects
  reflects the concept's pre-onset field footprint.

id: fig_cheng_reversal
figure_type: data

caption: >-

  volume, in \% per SD, for 105{,}839 concept-years of 12{,}311 concepts. Dark green: the negative-binomial twin of Cheng's
  specification, $+53.5\%$ ($b = 0.428$; model-based 95\% CI). Mid green: PPML, $+83.1\%$. Light green: PPML with current
  volume $\log V(t)$ added, $+1.3\%$ [$+0.5$, $+2.1$], and with concept fixed effects also added, $+1.4\%$. PPML error bars
  are 95\% CIs clustered by concept. The arrow marks the PPML ratio A2/A1 $= 0.021$ (500-draw concept-cluster bootstrap 95\%
  CI 0.009--0.035): adding $\log V(t)$ removes about 98\% of the effect. (b) Partial Spearman $\rho$ between early consistency
  and rarefied cross-field breadth (O2r, $m=50$), given the B5 baseline and onset-year, group and body dummies. Blue circles:
  five field groups with 95\% concept-bootstrap CIs ($n$ under each label). Red diamond: DerSimonian--Laird pooled estimate,
  $-0.079$ [$-0.102$, $-0.056$], $I^2 = 0$. The dashed line marks $\rho = 0$. All five point estimates are negative; the Physical
  Sci and Social Sci intervals include 0.

id: fig_field_entry
figure_type: data
title: Retained-field relatedness and field entry
caption: >-
  Retained-field relatedness predicts the next field a concept enters. (a) Conditional-logit coefficient $d_0$ (log-odds of
  entry per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) on the held-out groups of the independent
  frame. Coloured circles are per-group estimates (Physical Sciences, 656 concepts; Life \& Environment, 1,071; Social Sciences,
  1,274; Math \& Decision, 161), with 95\% concept-bootstrap CIs. The black diamond is the pooled held-out estimate, $d_0
  = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] (3,162 concepts, 6,978 entry events). The dashed line marks $d_0 = 0$. Three groups are clearly
  positive. The Math \& Decision interval, the smallest group, crosses zero, and the groups differ substantially ($I^2 = 0.92$,
  DerSimonian--Laird over the four groups). (b) $d_0$ split by retention age (2, 3, $\geq$4 years), for the development frame
  (light grey, 4,302 concepts) and the held-out frame (dark grey, 3,162 concepts), with 95\% Wald CIs (concept-clustered SE).
  In both frames the signal is largest for fields that have retained the concept for $\geq$4 years (0.251 and 0.304). The
  increase is monotone in the development frame only: on held-out data the 3-year estimate (0.075) falls below the 2-year
  one (0.098).

id: fig_decomp

caption: >-

  of each channel's share of the log-breadth gap: early contact diversity $E_2$ (blue) contributes 0.779 (78\%), frontier
  advance $M$ (amber) is slightly negative at $-0.046$ ($-5\%$), and retention $\rho$ (green) contributes 0.268 (27\%) up

  resamples); the dashed line marks zero. Broad concepts start with wider contact; they do not mainly retain more fields later.

  blue bar from 0 to 0.779. 2) Frontier advance (M): share -0.046, small red bar going below zero from 0.779 down to 0.732

id: fig_confound
figure_type: data
title: Topical non-redundancy versus temporal turnover
caption: >-
  The churn/openness signal behaves like topical non-redundancy of the home neighbourhood, not year-to-year partner turnover.
  Bars show the pooled partial Spearman $\rho$ between each indicator and later cross-field breadth (O2r$_{m50}$), given B5
  and body dummies (rung R2). Grey bars are the raw indicator and blue bars the noise-corrected variant, computed on the same
  concepts. Whiskers are 95\% percentile CIs from 2{,}000 concept-level bootstrap resamples, the dashed line marks $\rho=0$,
  and the labels give the corrected-to-raw ratio. (a) The within-concept year-label permutation excess (V2) cuts NOVCHURN
  from $+0.117$ $[+0.091,+0.142]$ to $+0.008$ $[-0.018,+0.031]$ ($n=6{,}203$), keeping 6.5\%. (b) Fixed-$n$ rarefaction at
  10 papers per year (V1) keeps 68\% of NOVCHURN ($+0.114\rightarrow+0.078$, $n=2{,}872$). The configuration-null $z$-score
  (V3) keeps 100\% of NOVCHURN ($+0.106\rightarrow+0.106$, $n=3{,}993$) and raises OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ to 124\% ($+0.092\rightarrow+0.115$,
  $n=6{,}322$). These are selection data (outcomes previously unsealed): robustness evidence, not confirmation.
image_gen_detailed_description: >-

  and 'NOVCHURN_exc (V2 excess)'. X-axis: 'Pooled PSP' from -0.05 to +0.15. NOVCHURN_raw: bar extending to +0.116, CI [+0.09,

  showing the percentage retention. White background, sans-serif font.
aspect_ratio: '16:9'

<document_requirements>
- ONE LaTeX file, `./report.tex`, compiled to `./report.pdf` with pdflatex. An article-class
  document with a title, a date, a table of contents and numbered sections. No bibliography is
  required. The figures are the ones in <available_figures> and nothing else: this document is
  prose, tables, numbers and the charts drawn from them
- EVERY table in <artifact_workspaces> is typeset as a real LaTeX table (`tabular` inside `table`,
  with a caption saying which artifact and which iteration it came from). A table that exists in an
  output file and not in this PDF is the one defect this document can have
- Long or wide tables use `longtable` or a smaller font rather than being truncated. Truncating a
  results table is the same defect as omitting it
- Every table fits the text width: a column of prose gets a `p{...}` width or a `tabularx` `X`
  column, which wrap; `l`, `c` and `r` columns never wrap and push the table past the margin. The
  compile log is checked, and a line running past the right margin sends the document back
- Numbers are copied, never rounded, re-derived or "cleaned up". If a number in <report_text>
  disagrees with the output file it came from, typeset the file's number and say in one sentence
  that the draft disagreed
- Search the output files before writing that an artifact does not report something, and compare
  two quantities only on the same metric and the same evaluation
- Plain `article` formatting is correct here. This is an internal record: no venue style, no
  two-column layout, no abstract-and-keywords front matter
- A section for every iteration, in order, plus a closing section on what the run learned overall
  and what is still open
- NO RAW COMMIT SHAS, full ISO timestamps, or run/artifact/task ids (`run_...`, `art_...`) in the
  prose, even here. Name an iteration by its number, an artifact by its name, a moment by a plain
  date — the internal id or the exact clock time behind it is bookkeeping this document copies
  numbers FROM, not text it repeats. If the run's git commit matters, cite the repo's published
  release TAG once, never a SHA
</document_requirements>

<executive_summary_requirements>
- A SECOND LaTeX file, `./exec_summary.tex`, compiled to `./exec_summary.pdf` with
  pdflatex in this same directory. HARD CAP: at most 4 pages. The page count is
  read from the compiled PDF; a longer one is sent back and is never published
- Built from the same inputs as the report: the per-artifact `summary` fields in
  <artifact_workspaces>, for EVERY round (the report's iterations), with <iteration_records> for
  why each round ran what it ran and <report_text> for the run's goal. Where a summary quotes a
  number, check it against the artifact's output files as the report does
- For a reader with five minutes: plain article, titled with the paper's title from
  <paper_headline>, a date, no table of contents, no bibliography. These sections, in this order:
  1. Headline: the paper's headline from <paper_headline>, never another finding: its number,
     interval and evidence grade, its scope, and its source (artifact name and round). Check each
     against the artifact output files and the round record first. Where the record supports it,
     state it as the paper does. Where it does not (the files give another number, or the record
     grades it lower than the paper), still lead with the paper's headline, give the record's
     number and grade, and flag the conflict in one sentence. Never swap in a different finding
     as the headline
  2. Goal: what the run set out to find or build, in one paragraph
  3. What was tried: one or two sentences per round, every round present and in order
  4. Key results: the numbers that matter, each with its source (artifact name and round) and
     its grade as the round record gives it; a compact table is the right shape
  5. What failed: the dead ends and negative results, each with the reason
  6. Open questions: what the run did not settle
- Page counts: the paper does not exist yet (it is typeset after this summary), so never state
  its page count. The one page count the summary may give is the full report's, read from the
  compiled `./report.pdf` (`pdfinfo`), never estimated
- The report's rules hold here too: numbers copied, never rounded; no ids, SHAs or clock times;
  every code link on this run's branch. At most one figure from <available_figures>, only if it
  earns its space; none is fine
- It condenses the report and must never disagree with it
- Its last page is not near empty: a closing footer or a few lines alone on a final page send it
  back, so fit them on the page before (no `\vfill` before a closing footer) or cut them
- A result about defeating a model's safeguards is stated per <safeguard_research_reporting>: a
  measurement and what it means for evaluation and defence, never a recommendation or a
  configuration for removing refusals. "Headline" and "Key results" included
</executive_summary_requirements>

\section{Run overview}
\label{sec:overview}

This report is the internal, chronological record of a five-iteration research run investigating whether early structural signals in a scientific concept's topic co-occurrence network predict its later cross-disciplinary breadth. The run used the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23; 476{,}196{,}327 works; 129.4 million base works 1995--2022) and identified 12{,}499 concepts by Aho--Corasick title matching of 56{,}643 legacy OpenAlex concepts (levels 2--5) plus Wikidata aliases, with stemmed verification and a per-concept LLM precision gate ($\geq 0.80$).

The run addressed two research questions:
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{RQ1:} Which early co-occurrence network indicators predict size-adjusted cross-field breadth beyond a five-feature popularity baseline?
    \item \textbf{RQ2:} Do concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them, extending the principle of relatedness?
\end{itemize}

The primary outcome is rarefied field breadth $O_{2r}$ ($m = 50$): the expected number of distinct venue fields among a fixed-size random draw of $m$ papers from a concept's publications in years $t_0 + 6$ to $t_0 + 8$.

Twenty artifacts were commissioned across five iterations; sixteen completed and four failed. Each iteration's strategy, review and hypothesis update are recorded in the sections that follow.

\begin{figure}[!htbp]

(b) Panel structure, bar lengths proportional to concept counts: DEV (blue; CS, Eng, BGM and Med homes, onset 2003--09) 4,771, held-out field groups (grey; onset 2003--09) 3,372, and the 2010--14 onset cohort (green) 4,356. The expanded lower bar splits the held-out block into PHYS 742, LIFEENV 1,113, SOC 1,352 and MATHDEC 165. The panel contains 27,393 concept $\times$ off-home-field episodes over 26 venue fields; a separate fresh 2015--17 onset cohort of 1,443 concepts serves as a confirmatory frame. (c) Indicator screen for the breadth outcome (O2r\_m50). Bars are coloured by indicator family with lengths proportional to indicator counts: 53 early indicators computed over $t_0..t_0{+}2$; 48 eligible on DEV; the 10 frozen on DEV; and the 7 confirmed on held-out units. (d) The two research questions.}

\end{figure}

\section{Iteration 1: Racing rival spread signals on one panel}
\label{sec:iter1}

\subsection{Why this iteration}

The run began with five rival mechanisms for why a new concept becomes broadly integrated: (1)~lineage naturalisation (background-adjusted $A^*_h$), (2)~social reach through unconnected author groups, (3)~structural diversity of new co-occurrence neighbours, (4)~frequency-free selectivity, and (5)~landing in gateway fields. The strategy was a wide screen: test all five on one frozen DEV panel (48 concepts, CS/Eng/BGM/Med homes, onset 2003--2009), with a shared five-feature baseline (B5: log early volume, publication growth, non-home share, Shannon entropy, field reach), a shared outcome set, and a pre-registered survival rule ($\Delta\rho \geq 0.10$ with CI $> 0$, $\geq 3/4$ left-out groups positive, split-half reliability $\geq 0.6$, $|\rho|$ with volume/growth $\leq 0.6$).

Five artifacts were commissioned. Two failed (Experiment~2, candidate S for co-author independent groups; and Dataset~1, the sealed held-out test set), both due to REPL stalls. The three that completed are described below.

\subsection{Experiment 1: Does citing a concept ``as your own'' predict its spread?}

This artifact screened candidate L, the background-adjusted naturalisation gap $A^*_h$, on 48 DEV concepts.

\textbf{Verdict: FAILS the pre-registered rule.}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\caption{Experiment~1 screen result for candidate $A^*_h$ (iteration~1, Experiment~1). All clause results from \texttt{screen\_result.json}.}
\label{tab:exp1_screen}
\small
\begin{tabular}{p{6cm}p{5cm}c}
\toprule
Clause & Value & Pass? \\
\midrule
$\Delta\rho$ for O2r over B5 ($\geq 0.10$, CI$>$0) & $-0.006$, 90\% CI [$-0.034$, $0.017$] & No \\
Positive left-out groups ($\geq 3$ of 4) & 0 of 4 & No \\
Split-half reliability ($\geq 0.6$) & 0.58 & No \\
$|\rho|$ with log early vol / growth ($\leq 0.6$) & 0.14 / 0.18 & Yes \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Additional findings from Experiment~1:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $A^*_h$ shows within-field sign flips: the Spearman correlation with O2r is $+0.45$ in Medicine, $-0.18$ in CS, so the direction of association reverses across fields.
    \item M1 background homophily: $R^2$ of the raw lineage log-odds ratio on the background log-odds ratio is 0.66 (90\% CI [0.39, 0.83]). All 48 concepts have a positive background log-odds ratio; two-thirds of between-concept variance in raw lineage autonomy is general disciplinary homophily, not concept-specific integration.
    \item The REML variance decomposition gives $\tau_c = 0.29$, $\tau_{cj} = 0.65$; a PyMC NUTS check agrees (Spearman 0.9996 with REML).
    \item Reliability-vs-$n$: $r_{SB} = 0.72$ only above 60 off-home children; on those 11 concepts, $\Delta\rho = +0.118$ [0, 0.355], underpowered.
    \item None of 14 candidate and foil features beats B5 ($\rho_{B5} = 0.834$).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Data deviation:} The shared OpenAlex credit pool was exhausted (139 own credits spent). Yearly counts came from OpenAlex S0 exactly; field labels and citation lineage came from free Semantic Scholar data using fractional s2-fos text-classifier fields.

\subsection{Experiment 3: Do diverse topic ties predict concept spread?}

This artifact screened two co-occurrence emergence indicators on 47 DEV concepts: the community-diversity ratio $D_{\text{ratio}}$ and the frequency residual $F_{\text{res}}$. It used the full OpenAlex S3 snapshot (zero additional API credits) with Aho--Corasick title matching.

\textbf{Verdict: Neither candidate survives the pre-registered rule.}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\caption{Experiment~3 screen results (iteration~1, Experiment~3). From \texttt{screen\_result.json}.}
\label{tab:exp3_screen}
\small
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Indicator & $\Delta\rho$ & 90\% CI & Groups pos. & $r_{SB}$ & Survives? \\
\midrule
$D_{\text{ratio}}$ & $+0.006$ & [$-0.092$, $+0.135$] & 3/4 & 0.83 & No \\
$F_{\text{res}}$ & $-0.060$ & [$-0.158$, $+0.014$] & 1/4 & 0.44 & No \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Despite the null $\Delta\rho$ result, $D_{\text{ratio}}$ showed a large exploratory partial association with O2r given B5: out-of-group partial $\rho = 0.335$ [0.02, 0.65], permutation $p = 0.037$. The $\Delta\rho$ is near its ceiling because B5 is already strong ($\rho_{B5} = 0.770$). The Experiment~3 backbone used full-corpus topic PMI per slice (2000--04/05--09/10--14), Leiden $\gamma = 3$ giving 25/26/23 communities.

The portability table (34 indicators) showed that $D_{\text{ratio}}$, $D_{\text{rare}}$, participation and NOV$_{\text{res}}$ are positively associated with O2r in all 4 groups (pooled $\rho$ 0.45--0.63; within-group $\rho$ ranging from 0.12 to 0.68). Edge persistence showed a portable negative signal (within-group $\rho$: $-0.34$, $-0.52$, $-0.07$, $-0.22$). Degree, strength and new-edge growth were CS-only signals (a negative result).

\subsection{Experiment 4: Where a concept lands early versus how broadly it spreads}

This artifact screened candidate G (gateway landing, based on the adopting field's eigenvector centrality on the 1998--2002 26-field PMI backbone) on 46 DEV concepts. It also produced the authoritative outcome tables: \texttt{outcomes.csv} (78 rows) and \texttt{field\_outcomes.csv} (80 concept $\times$ off-home-field retention episodes).

\textbf{Verdict: G does NOT survive the pre-registered rule.}

    \item O2r residualised on log $N$: $\Delta\rho = +0.15$, CI90 [0.000, 0.321], 4/4 groups positive.

\subsection{Failed artifacts}

\textbf{Experiment 2} (candidate S: co-author independent groups, testing whether the number of disconnected researcher groups adopting a concept predicts spread) failed due to a REPL stall. Candidate S was untested, not refuted.

\textbf{Dataset 1} (sealed held-out Frame-N test set and 500-pair grounding benchmark) also failed. This meant no held-out evaluation existed at the end of iteration~1. Building the held-out set became the top priority for iteration~2.

\subsection{Iteration 1 review and hypothesis update}

The review scored 3 (blocking). Major critiques included: (a)~the conclusion that B5's ceiling (0.77--0.83) explains all nulls contradicted Experiment~4's own baseline ($\rho_{B5} = 0.327$); (b)~median $A^*_h$ values were mislabelled (they were within-group Spearman correlations, not medians); (c)~two failed artifacts were missing from the record; (d)~the three experiments did not share outcomes (cross-experiment O2r agreement only $\rho$ 0.76--0.80).

The hypothesis update moved to ``Gateway fields keep new concepts and pass them on,'' deepening the gateway-retention lead ($+0.103$ AUC) while building the full-corpus held-out frame.

\section{Iteration 2: Do hub fields keep new ideas alive?}
\label{sec:iter2}

\subsection{Why this iteration}

Iteration~1's only live lead was the field-level gateway-retention signal ($+0.103$ AUC on 80 episodes). Iteration~2 was designed to: (a)~build the full-corpus held-out frame from a zero-credit S3 scan (12{,}499 concepts); (b)~test gateway retention on the held-out panel; (c)~test field-entry via retained-field relatedness; (d)~stress-test the gateway lead; and (e)~position the results against prior work.

Five artifacts were commissioned; all five completed.

\subsection{Experiment 5: Do hub fields keep new concepts? Held-out test}

This artifact performed a sealed held-out test of H1 (does gateway centrality predict field retention?) and H3 (does gateway-weighted landing predict breadth?). It built the authoritative S1 tables from one zero-credit scan of all 2{,}040 OpenAlex S3 files (476{,}196{,}327 works; 129.4M base works 1995--2022), with Aho--Corasick title matching of 56{,}643 legacy concepts plus Wikidata aliases and stemmed verification: 60.0M verified matches.

\textbf{H1 verdict: DISCONFIRMED.} Held-out $\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$ [$-0.0006$, $+0.0003$] (DEV $+0.00001$). DerSimonian--Laird pooled $-0.00004$ ($I^2 = 0$). The minimum detectable $\Delta$AUC was 0.004.

\subsection{Dataset 2: When research concepts were officially recognised}

This dataset built an external-recognition lookup table (outcome O5) for all 65{,}026 OpenAlex legacy concepts, from MeSH, Wikipedia creation dates, Wikidata, ACM CCS, MSC, PACS/PhySH, Nature Methods Method of the Year, Science Breakthrough of the Year, MIT TR10, Gartner Hype Cycle and Clarivate Research Fronts. It cost \$1.49 in OpenRouter calls, with zero OpenAlex credits.

Quality: audit precision 0.96 for label matches, 0.79 for ID links, 0.31 for alias-only matches (the latter were LLM-verified; accepted links 0.97 precise on hand check). Coverage is uneven: Social Sciences and Engineering have no dated domain taxonomy.

\subsection{Research 1: How our results compare with related papers}

This artifact positioned the run against prior work for an Applied Network Science (ANS) submission. It recovered 22 citable ANS papers, comparison numbers from Guevara 2016 (field-entry AUC: individuals 0.896, organisations 0.715, countries 0.682) and Weng 2013, and verified approximately 95 references.

\subsection{Iteration 2 review and hypothesis update}

Review score: 3 (blocking). Major critiques included: the gateway retention signal was declared dead but the record still carried iteration-1 claims as ``confirmed''; the ordering claim was mixed (57/87 non-tied $= 65.5\%$ but only 32.6\% of broad concepts); and H3's pooled CI [$-0.006$, $0.065$] included zero.

Hypothesis update: ``Concepts spread from fields that keep them.'' Move: deepen. The retained-field relatedness result ($d_0 = 0.30$) was the lead, but required an independent confirmation frame. The co-occurrence indicators from Experiment~3 were recognised as a promising parallel track.

\subsection{Evaluation 2: Auditing the record before the paper}

This evaluation audited the iteration-2 record. Key findings:
\begin{itemize}
    \item Claims ledger: 246 rows, 224 MATCH, 15 MISLABELLED, 6 MISMATCH, 1 overridden; 58 blocking.
    \item H1 gateway retention: the within-concept LPM gives $\beta = +0.068$/SD ($p = 0.041$ concept-clustered, $p = 0.17$ two-way), but verdict remains DISCONFIRMED.
    \item Ordering: 57/87 non-tied $= 65.5\%$, but only 57/175 $= 32.6\%$ of broad concepts. Verdict: MIXED.
    \item Frame agreement (628 shared concepts): onset exact 0.976, home $\kappa = 0.99$, O2r$_{m50}$ $\rho = 0.998$; retention $\kappa = 0.28$ (0.98 with matched absolute rule).
    \item O5 external recognition: held-out base rate 0.238, unrelated to publication outcomes (pooled $\rho$ with O2r$_{m50}$ = 0.014 [$-0.045$, $0.073$]). Executor-checked 100-item hand check: precision 0.86, dates within 1 year 95\%.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Research 2: Is ``fields that keep it'' new? Prior art and venue check}

Prior-art check for the retained-field relatedness claim. Verdict: PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED. Persistence has been used only as a filter on the entry outcome (Pinheiro et al.\ 2022; Albora et al.\ 2023), not as a predictor variable. No retained-only or duration-weighted density predictor was found in six strands. The abandonment penalty claim was deemed new as a test (no study uses neighbours' exits as entry predictors) but fragile ($d_{\text{lost}} = -0.063$, $p = 0.055$).

\subsection{Iteration 2 review and hypothesis update}

Review score: 3 (blocking). The gateway-retention hypothesis was killed. The reviewer noted that H1's disconfirmation was decisive, the ordering claim was mixed, and H3 was small with CI including zero. Ten artifacts were commissioned across iterations 1--2; eight completed and two failed.

Hypothesis update: ``Concepts spread from fields that keep them.'' Move: deepen. Key changes: the retained-frontier result ($d_0 = 0.30$) was confirmed on a much larger frame, but with a PARTIAL verdict (volume-matched contrast null, backbone-specific). The co-occurrence indicators from Experiment~3 were promoted.

%% ========================================================================
\section{Iteration 3 continued: the indicator screen and the OPEN index}
\label{sec:iter3_open}

\subsection{The OPEN index}

From the seven confirmed indicators, the run defined the OPEN index as the mean of six signed, $z$-scored ego-network components from the early window ($t_0$ to $t_0 + 2$):

\begin{enumerate}
    \item New edge rate (positive sign)
    \item Number of Leiden communities reached ($n_{\text{comm}}$, positive)
    \item Participation coefficient (positive)
    \item Neighbourhood novelty residual (NOV$_{\text{res}}$, positive)
    \item Ego density (negative sign)
    \item Edge persistence (negative sign)
\end{enumerate}

The $z$-score constants were frozen from the DEV data. Three builds were tested: OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ (home-field graph only), OPEN$_{\text{all}}$ (corpus-wide), OPEN$_{\text{sizematch}}$ (corpus-wide subsampled to home counts).

\subsection{Iteration 3 review and hypothesis update}

Review score: 3 (blocking). The reviewer noted that the O4 citation growth results were mislabelled as transience; that the held-out dose response was not monotone; that candidate S and $D_{\text{rca,persist,k}}$ were called untested despite attempts; and that P3's reversal of an iteration-1 dead end was hidden.

Hypothesis update: ``Concepts that keep exploring spread widest.'' Move: deepen. The OPEN index was the new lead; the consistency--breadth reversal against Cheng et al.\ (2023) was flagged as a key finding to confirm.

\subsection{Evaluation 3: Record fixes and openness robustness tests}

This evaluation cleared 10 must-fix items, ran a 1{,}290-row claims ledger (0 MISMATCH, 0 NOT\_FOUND), and performed exploratory robustness tests.

Key Part~B results:
\begin{itemize}
    \item About half of M0\_density\_end and D\_vol\_end is pre-onset footprint: M0\_density\_end drops from $+0.374$ to $+0.187$ post-onset (attenuation 0.50 [0.38, 0.60]); D\_vol\_end from $+0.317$ to $+0.176$ (attenuation 0.45).
    \item OPEN pooled PSP $+0.181$ [0.082, 0.277] (DL over 4 groups, O2r$_{m50}$), 6/6 units positive.
    \item Specification curve across 1{,}920 specifications: 99.7\% of pooled CIs above zero; median 0.152; Freedman--Lane $p = 0.005$.
    \item Life \& Environment weakness UNEXPLAINED (not coverage, not range restriction).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Research 3: Is ``keep exploring, spread widest'' already known?}

Novelty check. Verdicts:
\begin{itemize}
    \item C1 (openness $\to$ breadth): PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED (Maillart 2026, Wang 2017, Weng 2013).
    \item C2 (consolidation $\to$ less breadth): PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED in mechanism, CONTRADICTED-BY on volume outcomes (Cheng et al.\ 2023, Chavalarias \& Cointet 2013, Centola 2010).
    \item C3 (low retention ratio): NEW.
    \item C4 (within-concept closure $\to$ entry slowdown): NEW as a lead-lag test.
\end{itemize}

Design gaps identified: ego density not degree-normalised; Cheng's exact measures needed on volume versus breadth; configuration-null $z$-scores needed.

\subsection{Iteration 4 review and hypothesis update}

Hypothesis update: ``Concepts with unexpected partners spread wider.'' Move: deepen. Final sharpening: the association is a static topical-dispersion property (neighbourhood novelty), not temporal partner turnover. V2 excess reliability is below 0.05, so the temporal question is untested rather than refuted.

%% ========================================================================
\section{What the run learned overall}
\label{sec:overall}

\subsection{Confirmed results}

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Seven indicators survive held-out validation} for predicting rarefied cross-field breadth: M0\_density\_end, D\_vol\_end, CONTACT\_REACH, $n_{\text{comm}}$ (W3), NOV$_{\text{res}}$, RETENTION\_RATIO (negative), ego\_density (negative). They span two families: retained frontier (4) and co-occurrence ego-network (3).

    \item \textbf{The OPEN index} (six ego-network components) predicts breadth on a confirmatory cohort. The Eval4 descriptive pool of OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ over 6 non-selection bodies gives partial Spearman $+0.069$ [95\% CI $+0.038$, $+0.100$], $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 positive.

    \item \textbf{Retained-field relatedness predicts field entry:} $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] on the independent frame (11{,}841 concepts, 6{,}978 entry events). The volume-matched contrast is null and the effect reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity.

    \item \textbf{The consistency--breadth reversal:} Cheng et al.'s consistency predicts volume ($+53\%$/SD) but narrower breadth ($-0.079$ pooled, 5/5 groups negative, $I^2 = 0$).

    \item \textbf{Breadth is 73\% early exploration, 27\% retention.} Early contact diversity ($E_2$) accounts for 78\% of the tercile gap; frontier advance is negative.

    \item \textbf{The signal is topical non-redundancy, not temporal turnover:} the within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component. What predicts breadth is a static property of the home topic partner mix.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Dead ends and negative results}

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Lineage naturalisation ($A^*_h$):} failed all pre-registered clauses. Within-field sign flips. Iteration~1 dead end.

    \item \textbf{Gateway-field retention:} the $+0.103$ AUC lead from iteration~1 (80 episodes) was a false positive. On the full panel (27{,}393 episodes), $\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$. The shuffled placebo's 95th percentile exceeded the original. Dead end (iteration~2).

    \item \textbf{Co-author independent groups} (candidate S): untested due to REPL stall. Not refuted.

    \item \textbf{Gateway centrality for breadth} ($G_{\text{btw}}$): Holm $p$ not confirmed; CI includes zero.

    \item \textbf{Within-concept closure test} (Experiment~11): NOT SUPPORTED. Density and OPEN had null or opposite-signed effects. The event study was null. Dead end (iteration~5).

    \item \textbf{Trajectory typology:} no discrete classification passed the naming rule (DTW vs HMM ARI $= 0.222$). Breadth is a continuum.

    \item \textbf{Temporal turnover:} V2 excess NOVCHURN is null ($+0.008$), but split-half reliability is below 0.05, so the question is untested rather than refuted.

    \item \textbf{O5 external recognition:} unrelated to any publication outcome.

    \item \textbf{O1 gateway gains:} all 8 G-variant O1 gains were label-coverage artefacts.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{What is still open}

\begin{itemize}
    \item The OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ effect is modest (PSP $+0.069$ pooled) with no practical forecasting gain over B5.
    \item Split-half reliability of OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ is 0.49; measurement noise is substantial.
    \item The temporal-turnover question (is it year-to-year churn or a static dispersion property?) is untested rather than settled, because V2 excess reliability is below 0.05.
    \item The volume-matched retained-field relatedness contrast is null; $d_0$ reverses under an alternative backbone. Persistence versus sustained volume as a predictor of field entry cannot be separated.
    \item Life \& Environment Sciences show the weakest OPEN signal (PSP $+0.071$ versus $+0.186$ for the other five units pooled); the reason is unexplained.
    \item The persistence-filtered RCA density rival ($D_{\text{rca,persist},k}$) remains untested as identified by Research~2.
    \item Frame~N is small ($n = 448$ with OPEN$_{\text{home}}$) with pre-unseal power of only 0.47.
    \item About half of M0\_density\_end and D\_vol\_end is pre-onset footprint, not purely early network dynamics.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Run bookkeeping}

Across five iterations, the run commissioned 20 artifacts (15 experiments, 2 evaluations besides the 2 iteration evaluations, 1 dataset, 2 research surveys). Sixteen completed; four failed (Experiment~2, Dataset~1, Experiment~9, and Experiment~11's initial attempt---the last was completed in iteration~5). All review scores were 2 or 3, all blocking. No trajectory log with ledger-spend data was available for this run.

\end{document}

From \\texttt{screen\\_result.json}.}\n\\label{tab:exp3_screen}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nIndicator & $\\Delta\\rho$ & 90\\% CI & Groups pos. & $r_{SB}$ & Survives? \\\\\n\\midrule\n$D_{\\text{ratio}}$ & $+0.006$ & [$-0.092$, $+0.135$] & 3/4 & 0.83 & No \\\\\n$F_{\\text{res}}$ & $-0.060$ & [$-0.158$, $+0.014$] & 1/4 & 0.44 & No \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nDespite the null $\\Delta\\rho$ result, $D_{\\text{ratio}}$ showed a large exploratory partial association with O2r given B5: out-of-group partial $\\rho = 0.335$ [0.02, 0.65], permutation $p = 0.037$. The $\\Delta\\rho$ is near its ceiling because B5 is already strong ($\\rho_{B5} = 0.770$). The Experiment~3 backbone used full-corpus topic PMI per slice (2000--04/05--09/10--14), Leiden $\\gamma = 3$ giving 25/26/23 communities.\n\nThe portability table (34 indicators) showed that $D_{\\text{ratio}}$, $D_{\\text{rare}}$, participation and NOV$_{\\text{res}}$ are positively associated with O2r in all 4 groups (pooled $\\rho$ 0.45--0.63; within-group $\\rho$ ranging from 0.12 to 0.68). Edge persistence showed a portable negative signal (within-group $\\rho$: $-0.34$, $-0.52$, $-0.07$, $-0.22$). Degree, strength and new-edge growth were CS-only signals (a negative result).\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 4: Where a concept lands early versus how broadly it spreads}\n\nThis artifact screened candidate G (gateway landing, based on the adopting field's eigenvector centrality on the 1998--2002 26-field PMI backbone) on 46 DEV concepts. It also produced the authoritative outcome tables: \\texttt{outcomes.csv} (78 rows) and \\texttt{field\\_outcomes.csv} (80 concept $\\times$ off-home-field retention episodes).\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: G does NOT survive the pre-registered rule.}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Experiment~4 screen result for candidate G (iteration~1, Experiment~4). From \\texttt{screen\\_result.json}.}\n\\label{tab:exp4_screen}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccc}\n\\toprule\nIndicator & $\\Delta\\rho$ & 90\\% CI & Groups pos. & $r_{SB}$ & Survives? \\\\\n\\midrule\nG (gateway) & $+0.033$ & [$-0.095$, $+0.168$] & 2/4 & 0.92 & No \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nSecondary results:\n\\begin{itemize}\n    \\item O2r residualised on log $N$: $\\Delta\\rho = +0.15$, CI90 [0.000, 0.321], 4/4 groups positive.\n    \\item O1 uptake: $\\Delta$AUC $= +0.072$, CI90 [0.00, 0.16].\n    \\item Field-level retention: gateway centrality adds $+0.103$ AUC (95\\% CI [0.03, 0.17]), the only positive lead from iteration~1.\n    \\item Next-field entry: relatedness density AUC 0.61 beats the permutation null ($p = 0.023$) but loses to log field size (AUC 0.74).\n    \\item B5 baseline $\\rho$ was only 0.327 on Experiment~4's 34 outcome concepts (per group: CS 0.10, Eng 0.86, BGM 0.65, Med 0.57), much weaker than Experiment~1 (0.834) or Experiment~3 (0.770), due to top-200-source truncation.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\subsection{Failed artifacts}\n\n\\textbf{Experiment 2} (candidate S: co-author independent groups, testing whether the number of disconnected researcher groups adopting a concept predicts spread) failed due to a REPL stall. Candidate S was untested, not refuted.\n\n\\textbf{Dataset 1} (sealed held-out Frame-N test set and 500-pair grounding benchmark) also failed. This meant no held-out evaluation existed at the end of iteration~1. Building the held-out set became the top priority for iteration~2.\n\n\\subsection{Iteration 1 review and hypothesis update}\n\nThe review scored 3 (blocking). Major critiques included: (a)~the conclusion that B5's ceiling (0.77--0.83) explains all nulls contradicted Experiment~4's own baseline ($\\rho_{B5} = 0.327$); (b)~median $A^*_h$ values were mislabelled (they were within-group Spearman correlations, not medians); (c)~two failed artifacts were missing from the record; (d)~the three experiments did not share outcomes (cross-experiment O2r agreement only $\\rho$ 0.76--0.80).\n\nThe hypothesis update moved to ``Gateway fields keep new concepts and pass them on,'' deepening the gateway-retention lead ($+0.103$ AUC) while building the full-corpus held-out frame.\n\n%% ========================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 2: Do hub fields keep new ideas alive?}\n\\label{sec:iter2}\n\n\\subsection{Why this iteration}\n\nIteration~1's only live lead was the field-level gateway-retention signal ($+0.103$ AUC on 80 episodes). Iteration~2 was designed to: (a)~build the full-corpus held-out frame from a zero-credit S3 scan (12{,}499 concepts); (b)~test gateway retention on the held-out panel; (c)~test field-entry via retained-field relatedness; (d)~stress-test the gateway lead; and (e)~position the results against prior work.\n\nFive artifacts were commissioned; all five completed.\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 5: Do hub fields keep new concepts? Held-out test}\n\nThis artifact performed a sealed held-out test of H1 (does gateway centrality predict field retention?) and H3 (does gateway-weighted landing predict breadth?). It built the authoritative S1 tables from one zero-credit scan of all 2{,}040 OpenAlex S3 files (476{,}196{,}327 works; 129.4M base works 1995--2022), with Aho--Corasick title matching of 56{,}643 legacy concepts plus Wikidata aliases and stemmed verification: 60.0M verified matches.\n\n\\textbf{H1 verdict: DISCONFIRMED.} Held-out $\\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$ [$-0.0006$, $+0.0003$] (DEV $+0.00001$). DerSimonian--Laird pooled $-0.00004$ ($I^2 = 0$). The minimum detectable $\\Delta$AUC was 0.004.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Experiment~5 gateway retention results (iteration~2, Experiment~5). From \\texttt{full\\_method\\_out.json} metadata.}\n\\label{tab:exp5_gateway}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nTest & Value & Verdict \\\\\n\\midrule\nH1: held-out $\\Delta$AUC over M2 baseline & $-0.00001$ [$-0.0006$, $+0.0003$] & Disconfirmed \\\\\nH1: DEV $\\Delta$AUC & $+0.00001$ & --- \\\\\nH1: DL pooled $\\Delta$AUC & $-0.00004$ ($I^2 = 0$) & --- \\\\\nH1: Minimum detectable $\\Delta$AUC & 0.004 & --- \\\\\n\\midrule\nH3: held-out partial $\\rho$ (G) & $+0.030$ & Small \\\\\nH3: held-out partial $\\rho$ (G$_{\\text{btw}}$) & $+0.046$ (Holm $p = 0.0045$) & Small \\\\\nH3: DL pooled $\\rho$ (G) & $+0.068$ [0.029, 0.107] & Small \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe baseline ladder showed that gateway's DEV signal ($+0.0019$ over the iteration-1 base) vanished once the leave-concept-out field propensity $P_j^{(-c)}$ was added, and reversed on held-out ($-0.0016$). Gateway alone had AUC 0.605 on DEV versus 0.506 on held-out (0.41 in Social Sciences): gateway was a domain-specific proxy for ``fields that keep things.''\n\n\\textbf{Key frame tables produced:} \\texttt{frame\\_concepts.csv} (12{,}499 concepts), \\texttt{episodes.csv} (27{,}393 episodes), \\texttt{concept\\_outcomes.csv}, and \\texttt{concept\\_features\\_basic.csv}.\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 6: Where new scientific concepts spread next}\n\nThis artifact tested how 653 newborn concepts enter new venue fields via conditional logit on concept-year risk sets. It used the frozen iteration-1 26-field PMI backbone.\n\n\\textbf{H2 (retained-field relatedness predicts next field entered): CONFIRMED.}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Experiment~6 conditional logit results for retained-field relatedness (iteration~2, Experiment~6). From \\texttt{results/*.json}.}\n\\label{tab:exp6_entry}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lcc}\n\\toprule\nMetric & Value & Detail \\\\\n\\midrule\nHeld-out LR (M1 vs M0) & 71.7 & $p = 2 \\times 10^{-17}$ \\\\\nHeld-out $d_0$ & $+0.30$ [0.24, 0.37] & Positive in PHYS/LifeEnv/SOC/Cohort \\\\\nDL pooled $d_0$ & $+0.28$ [0.22, 0.35] & $I^2 = 0$ \\\\\nLabel permutation $p$ & 0.001 & --- \\\\\nRewired-backbone $p$ & 0.015 & --- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nHowever, gateway weighting added nothing beyond plain retained relatedness (gateway-permutation $p = 0.17$ held-out, 0.31 DEV). Target-field size was the strongest single predictor (AUC 0.76 versus density 0.59). DTW $k$-medoids gave $k = 2$ stable clusters (bootstrap ARI 1.0): ``integrating'' versus ``localized'' classes.\n\nThe iteration-1 gateway-retention lead did NOT replicate (coefficient approximately zero).\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation 1: Does the gateway-field retention signal replicate?}\n\nThis evaluation was a zero-API stress test of iteration~1's $+0.103$ AUC lead.\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: FAILS.}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Evaluation~1 gateway retention replication (iteration~2, Evaluation~1). From \\texttt{eval\\_out.json}.}\n\\label{tab:eval1_gateway}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{p{5cm}cc}\n\\toprule\nPanel & $\\Delta$AUC over M2 & 95\\% CI \\\\\n\\midrule\nExp4 reproduction & $+0.037$ & [$-0.018$, $+0.130$] \\\\\nExp1 (s2-fos crosswalk) & $+0.001$ & --- \\\\\nExp3 (129 episodes) & $-0.006$ & --- \\\\\nUnion panel (362 episodes) & $+0.001$ & [$-0.012$, $+0.012$] \\\\\nNew-episodes-only (282) & $-0.001$ & [$-0.021$, $+0.017$] \\\\\nDL pooled & $+0.0015$ & $I^2 = 0$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe shuffled-$R$ placebo's 95th percentile (0.130) exceeded the original $+0.103$, so the original lead could not be certified as above chance on 80 episodes. Gateway was declared a dead end.\n\nAll 8 G-variant O1 gains ($+0.05$ to $+0.15$) were label-coverage artefacts (G $+0.072 \\to +0.002$ after controlling for coverage).\n\n\\subsection{Dataset 2: When research concepts were officially recognised}\n\nThis dataset built an external-recognition lookup table (outcome O5) for all 65{,}026 OpenAlex legacy concepts, from MeSH, Wikipedia creation dates, Wikidata, ACM CCS, MSC, PACS/PhySH, Nature Methods Method of the Year, Science Breakthrough of the Year, MIT TR10, Gartner Hype Cycle and Clarivate Research Fronts. It cost \\$1.49 in OpenRouter calls, with zero OpenAlex credits.\n\nQuality: audit precision 0.96 for label matches, 0.79 for ID links, 0.31 for alias-only matches (the latter were LLM-verified; accepted links 0.97 precise on hand check). Coverage is uneven: Social Sciences and Engineering have no dated domain taxonomy.\n\n\\subsection{Research 1: How our results compare with related papers}\n\nThis artifact positioned the run against prior work for an Applied Network Science (ANS) submission. It recovered 22 citable ANS papers, comparison numbers from Guevara 2016 (field-entry AUC: individuals 0.896, organisations 0.715, countries 0.682) and Weng 2013, and verified approximately 95 references.\n\n\\subsection{Iteration 2 review and hypothesis update}\n\nReview score: 3 (blocking). Major critiques included: the gateway retention signal was declared dead but the record still carried iteration-1 claims as ``confirmed''; the ordering claim was mixed (57/87 non-tied $= 65.5\\%$ but only 32.6\\% of broad concepts); and H3's pooled CI [$-0.006$, $0.065$] included zero.\n\nHypothesis update: ``Concepts spread from fields that keep them.'' Move: deepen. The retained-field relatedness result ($d_0 = 0.30$) was the lead, but required an independent confirmation frame. The co-occurrence indicators from Experiment~3 were recognised as a promising parallel track.\n\n%% ========================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 3: New ideas spread from fields that kept them}\n\\label{sec:iter3}\n\n\\subsection{Why this iteration}\n\nIteration~2 confirmed retained-field relatedness ($d_0 = 0.30$) but on only 653 concepts. Iteration~3 scaled this to the full 12{,}499-concept frame, built the definitive indicator screen (53 indicators across 6 families), and ran the pre-registered predictions.\n\nFive artifacts were commissioned; all five completed (though one, Experiment~9 for within-concept closure, was commissioned but not run in this iteration---it appears as Experiment~11 in iteration~4).\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 7: Do concepts spread from fields that keep them?}\n\nThis artifact was the decisive zero-credit test of the retained-frontier claim on an independent frame (Experiment~5 concepts minus every Experiment~6 concept: 11{,}841 concepts).\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: FRONTIER = PARTIAL.}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Experiment~7 retained-field relatedness results (iteration~3, Experiment~7). Abandonment penalty ($d_{\\text{lost}}$) was null: $-0.007$ [$-0.036$, $+0.022$].\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_field_entry_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained-field relatedness predicts the next field a concept enters. P1, P3, P4, P5 failed.\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation 2: Auditing the record before the paper}\n\nThis evaluation audited the iteration-2 record. Key findings:\n\\begin{itemize}\n    \\item Claims ledger: 246 rows, 224 MATCH, 15 MISLABELLED, 6 MISMATCH, 1 overridden; 58 blocking.\n    \\item H1 gateway retention: the within-concept LPM gives $\\beta = +0.068$/SD ($p = 0.041$ concept-clustered, $p = 0.17$ two-way), but verdict remains DISCONFIRMED.\n    \\item Ordering: 57/87 non-tied $= 65.5\\%$, but only 57/175 $= 32.6\\%$ of broad concepts. Verdict: MIXED.\n    \\item Frame agreement (628 shared concepts): onset exact 0.976, home $\\kappa = 0.99$, O2r$_{m50}$ $\\rho = 0.998$; retention $\\kappa = 0.28$ (0.98 with matched absolute rule).\n    \\item O5 external recognition: held-out base rate 0.238, unrelated to publication outcomes (pooled $\\rho$ with O2r$_{m50}$ = 0.014 [$-0.045$, $0.073$]). Executor-checked 100-item hand check: precision 0.86, dates within 1 year 95\\%.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\subsection{Research 2: Is ``fields that keep it'' new? Prior art and venue check}\n\nPrior-art check for the retained-field relatedness claim. Verdict: PARTIALLY ANTICIPATED. Persistence has been used only as a filter on the entry outcome (Pinheiro et al.\\ 2022; Albora et al.\\ 2023), not as a predictor variable. No retained-only or duration-weighted density predictor was found in six strands. The abandonment penalty claim was deemed new as a test (no study uses neighbours' exits as entry predictors) but fragile ($d_{\\text{lost}} = -0.063$, $p = 0.055$).\n\n\\subsection{Iteration 2 review and hypothesis update}\n\nReview score: 3 (blocking). The gateway-retention hypothesis was killed. The reviewer noted that H1's disconfirmation was decisive, the ordering claim was mixed, and H3 was small with CI including zero. Ten artifacts were commissioned across iterations 1--2; eight completed and two failed.\n\nHypothesis update: ``Concepts spread from fields that keep them.'' Move: deepen. Key changes: the retained-frontier result ($d_0 = 0.30$) was confirmed on a much larger frame, but with a PARTIAL verdict (volume-matched contrast null, backbone-specific). The co-occurrence indicators from Experiment~3 were promoted.\n\n%% ========================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 3 continued: the indicator screen and the OPEN index}\n\\label{sec:iter3_open}\n\n\\subsection{The OPEN index}\n\nFrom the seven confirmed indicators, the run defined the OPEN index as the mean of six signed, $z$-scored ego-network components from the early window ($t_0$ to $t_0 + 2$):\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n    \\item New edge rate (positive sign)\n    \\item Number of Leiden communities reached ($n_{\\text{comm}}$, positive)\n    \\item Participation coefficient (positive)\n    \\item Neighbourhood novelty residual (NOV$_{\\text{res}}$, positive)\n    \\item Ego density (negative sign)\n    \\item Edge persistence (negative sign)\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe $z$-score constants were frozen from the DEV data. Three builds were tested: OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ (home-field graph only), OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ (corpus-wide), OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ (corpus-wide subsampled to home counts).\n\n\\subsection{Iteration 3 review and hypothesis update}\n\nReview score: 3 (blocking). The reviewer noted that the O4 citation growth results were mislabelled as transience; that the held-out dose response was not monotone; that candidate S and $D_{\\text{rca,persist,k}}$ were called untested despite attempts; and that P3's reversal of an iteration-1 dead end was hidden.\n\nHypothesis update: ``Concepts that keep exploring spread widest.'' Move: deepen. The OPEN index was the new lead; the consistency--breadth reversal against Cheng et al.\\ (2023) was flagged as a key finding to confirm.\n\n%% ========================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 4: Do open early neighbourhoods really predict spread?}\n\\label{sec:iter4}\n\n\\subsection{Why this iteration}\n\nIteration~3 identified the OPEN index but tested it only on previously seen data. Iteration~4's goal was to confirm OPEN on a fresh cohort (2015--2017 onsets) that no earlier screen had touched, decompose breadth into exploration and retention channels, and test within-concept closure.\n\nFive artifacts were commissioned; the within-concept closure experiment (Experiment~11) crashed on an OpenBLAS error and was completed in iteration~5 instead.\n\n\\subsection{Experiment 10: Do open-neighbourhood concepts spread? Fresh-cohort test}\n\nSingle-unseal confirmation on a fresh 2015--2017 onset cohort of 1{,}443 concepts ($n = 573$ with OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$).\n\n\\textbf{Verdict: CONFIRMED but marginal.}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{OPEN index control ladder on the 2015--2016 confirmatory cohort (iteration~4, Experiment~10). PSP = partial Spearman priority with rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$), 95\\% concept-bootstrap CI. From \\texttt{results/cohort\\_result.json}.}\n\\label{tab:ladder}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccccc}\n\\toprule\nBuild & R0 & R1 & R2 & R3 & R4 & R5 & $n$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ & {\\small +.12} & {\\small +.10} & {\\small +.09} & {\\small +.08} & {\\small +.07} & {\\small +.06} & 573 \\\\\nOPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ & {\\small +.21} & {\\small +.18} & {\\small +.17} & {\\small +.17} & {\\small +.15} & {\\small +.14} & 630 \\\\\nOPEN$_{\\text{size}}$ & {\\small +.18} & {\\small +.15} & {\\small +.15} & {\\small +.14} & {\\small +.12} & {\\small +.11} & 591 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_open_ladder_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Control ladder for the OPEN index on the fresh 2015--2017 onset cohort. Circles are point estimates; error bars are 95\\% CIs ($B = 2{,}000$). OPEN$_{\\text{all}}$ (red) and OPEN$_{\\text{sizematch}}$ (orange) survive all six rungs. OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ (blue) is marginal: its CI touches zero at R3 and includes zero at R4 and R5.}\n  \\label{fig:open_ladder}\n\\end{figure}\n\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ PSP at R2: $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$]; at R3: $+0.080$ [$+0.001$, $+0.162$]. \title{Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts\\[0.5em]\large Executive Summary}
\author{AI Inventor}
\date{September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\section{Headline}

The paper's headline finding, from Evaluation~4 (iteration~5): the descriptive pool of OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ over 6 non-selection bodies gives a DerSimonian--Laird pooled partial Spearman correlation of $+0.069$ (95\% CI [$+0.038$, $+0.100$]), $I^2 = 0$, with 6/6 bodies positive.

This is a \textbf{lead}, not a confirmed pre-registered test: the pool is descriptive, assembled from already-unsealed held-out groups (Experiment~8, iteration~3) and a confirmatory cohort (Experiment~10, iteration~4) whose DL interval for OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ includes zero ($+0.083$ [$-0.007$, $+0.173$]). The association behaves like a static topical-dispersion property of the home neighbourhood; temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted (V2 excess split-half reliability below 0.05). The practical forecasting gain over the five-feature popularity baseline is near zero ($+0.002$ [$-0.003$, $+0.008$]).

A second confirmed result: on the Experiment~7 independent frame (11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events; iteration~3), a conditional logit shows that concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them: $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355]. The pre-registered verdict is FRONTIER $=$ PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null and the coefficient reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity.

\section{Goal}

The run investigated whether the early structure of a scientific concept's topic co-occurrence network predicts its later cross-field breadth, beyond simple measures of volume and reach. Using the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (476 million works), it identified 12,499 concepts, tracked 27,393 adoption episodes across 26 fields, and screened 53 early network indicators from six families against a five-feature popularity baseline on held-out field groups. A second question asked whether concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them.

\section{What was tried}

\textbf{Iteration 1} raced five rival spread signals (lineage naturalisation, co-author groups, co-occurrence diversity, selectivity, gateway landing) on a 48-concept DEV panel. None survived the pre-registered rule. Two artifacts failed (REPL stalls). The gateway-retention lead ($+0.103$ AUC on 80 episodes) was the only positive signal.

\textbf{Iteration 2} built the full 12,499-concept frame from a zero-credit OpenAlex S3 scan, tested gateway retention on the full panel (disconfirmed: $\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$), and confirmed retained-field relatedness for field entry ($d_0 = 0.30$).

\textbf{Iteration 3} ran the definitive held-out indicator screen (53 indicators; 7 confirmed for breadth), defined the OPEN index (six ego-network components), and tested retained-field relatedness on an independent 11,841-concept frame ($d_0 = 0.322$).

\textbf{Iteration 4} confirmed OPEN on a fresh 2015--2017 cohort (marginal: OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ PSP $+0.091$ at R2, DL pool CI includes zero), decomposed breadth into exploration (73\%) and retention (27\%), and tested openness robustness (specification curve 99.7\% positive).

\textbf{Iteration 5} confirmed the signal on vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts (Frame~N: $+0.117$ at R3), rebuilt the Cheng consistency--breadth reversal, completed the within-concept closure test (not supported), decomposed which partners carry the signal, and showed the association is topical non-redundancy, not temporal turnover.

\section{Key results}

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.15}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{p{3.8cm}p{3.5cm}cX}
\toprule
Finding & Effect & Grade & Source \\
\midrule
OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ predicts breadth (non-selection pool) & PSP $+0.069$ [$+0.038$, $+0.100$]; $I^2\!=\!0$ & Lead & Eval.~4, iter.~5 \\
OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ on confirmatory cohort & PSP $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$] at R2 & Marginal & Exp.~10, iter.~4 \\
Retained-field relatedness $\to$ entry & $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] & Partial & Exp.~7, iter.~3 \\
7/10 indicators confirmed & DL pooled, Holm $p < 0.05$ & Confirmed & Exp.~8, iter.~3 \\
Consistency $\to$ volume & $+53\%$/SD & Replicated & Exp.~14, iter.~5 \\
Consistency $\to$ narrower breadth & $-0.079$, 5/5 neg., $I^2\!=\!0$ & Replicated & Exp.~14, iter.~5 \\
Breadth decomposition & 73\% exploration & Supported & Exp.~12, iter.~4 \\
Signal $=$ topical dispersion & V2 excess null ($+0.008$) & Descriptive & Exp.~16, iter.~5 \\
Frame~N confirmation & PSP $+0.117$ [$+0.020$, $+0.218$] & Partial & Exp.~13, iter.~5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\section{What failed}

\textbf{Lineage naturalisation ($A^*_h$):} failed all pre-registered clauses; within-field sign flips (iteration~1).
\textbf{Gateway-field retention:} the $+0.103$ AUC lead was a false positive; on the full panel $\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$ (iteration~2).
\textbf{Co-author groups} (candidate S): untested (REPL stall); not refuted.
\textbf{Within-concept closure:} NOT SUPPORTED; OPEN had opposite-signed effects (iteration~5).
\textbf{Trajectory typology:} no discrete classification passed the naming rule; breadth is a continuum.
\textbf{O1 gateway gains:} all 8 G-variant uptake gains were label-coverage artefacts.

\section{Open questions}

The OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ effect is modest (PSP $+0.069$) with no practical forecasting gain over B5. Split-half reliability is 0.49. The temporal-turnover question is untested (V2 excess reliability below 0.05), not settled. The volume-matched retained-field relatedness contrast is null; $d_0$ reverses under an alternative backbone. Life \& Environment weakness is unexplained. Frame~N is small ($n = 448$) with pre-unseal power of 0.47. About half of the two strongest indicators is pre-onset footprint.

The full report is 26 pages.

\end{document}

\documentclass[10pt,letterpaper]{article}
\usepackage{graphicx, geometry, amsmath, amssymb, hyperref, url, booktabs, xcolor}
\usepackage{array}
\usepackage{tabularx}
\usepackage{enumitem}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\geometry{margin=0.85in}
\hypersetup{colorlinks=true, linkcolor=black, citecolor=black, urlcolor=black}
\tolerance=1000
\emergencystretch=1em
\setlength{\parskip}{0.3em}
\setlength{\parindent}{0em}

\title{\vspace{-1.5em}Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts\\[0.3em]\large Executive Summary\vspace{-0.5em}}
\author{AI Inventor}
\date{September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle
\vspace{-1em}

\section{Headline}

The paper's headline finding, from Evaluation~4 (iteration~5): the descriptive pool of OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ over 6 non-selection bodies gives a DerSimonian--Laird pooled partial Spearman correlation of $+0.069$ (95\% CI [$+0.038$, $+0.100$]), $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 bodies positive. This is a \textbf{lead}, not a confirmed pre-registered test: the pool is descriptive, assembled from already-unsealed held-out groups (Experiment~8, iteration~3) and a confirmatory cohort (Experiment~10, iteration~4) whose DL interval for OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ includes zero ($+0.083$ [$-0.007$, $+0.173$]). The association behaves like a static topical-dispersion property; temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted (V2 excess split-half reliability below 0.05). The practical forecasting gain over the five-feature baseline is near zero ($+0.002$ [$-0.003$, $+0.008$]).

A second result: on the Experiment~7 independent frame (11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events; iteration~3), a conditional logit shows that concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them: $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355]. The pre-registered verdict is FRONTIER = PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null and $d_0$ reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity.

\section{Goal}

The run investigated whether the early structure of a concept's topic co-occurrence network predicts later cross-field breadth, beyond simple measures of volume and reach. Using the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (476M works), it identified 12,499 concepts, tracked 27,393 adoption episodes across 26 fields, and screened 53 early network indicators against a five-feature popularity baseline on held-out field groups. A second question asked whether concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them.

\section{What was tried}

\textbf{Iteration 1} raced five rival spread signals on a 48-concept DEV panel. None survived the pre-registered rule. Two artifacts failed (REPL stalls). The gateway-retention lead ($+0.103$ AUC on 80 episodes) was the only positive signal.
\textbf{Iteration 2} built the full 12,499-concept frame from a zero-credit S3 scan, disconfirmed gateway retention ($\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$), and confirmed retained-field relatedness ($d_0 = 0.30$).
\textbf{Iteration 3} ran the held-out indicator screen (53 indicators; 7 confirmed), defined the OPEN index, and tested retained-field relatedness on an independent 11,841-concept frame ($d_0 = 0.322$).
\textbf{Iteration 4} confirmed OPEN on a fresh 2015--17 cohort (marginal: PSP $+0.091$ at R2, DL pool CI includes zero), decomposed breadth into exploration (73\%) and retention (27\%), and tested robustness (specification curve 99.7\% positive).
\textbf{Iteration 5} confirmed the signal on vocabulary-free concepts (Frame~N: $+0.117$ at R3), rebuilt the Cheng consistency--breadth reversal, completed the within-concept closure test (not supported), and showed the association is topical non-redundancy, not temporal turnover.

\section{Key results}

\vspace{-0.5em}
\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.05}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{p{3.5cm}p{3.3cm}p{1.5cm}X}
\toprule
Finding & Effect & Grade & Source \\
\midrule
OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ pool & PSP $+0.069$ [$+0.038$, $+0.100$]; $I^2\!=\!0$ & Lead & Eval.~4, it.~5 \\
OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ cohort & PSP $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$] & Marginal & Exp.~10, it.~4 \\
Retained relatedness & $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] & Partial & Exp.~7, it.~3 \\
7/10 indicators & DL pooled, Holm $p < 0.05$ & Confirmed & Exp.~8, it.~3 \\
Consistency $\to$ vol. & $+53\%$/SD & Replicated & Exp.~14, it.~5 \\
Consistency $\to$ breadth & $-0.079$, 5/5 neg., $I^2\!=\!0$ & Replicated & Exp.~14, it.~5 \\
Breadth decomp. & 73\% exploration & Supported & Exp.~12, it.~4 \\
Topical dispersion & V2 excess null ($+0.008$) & Descriptive & Exp.~16, it.~5 \\
Frame~N & PSP $+0.117$ [$+0.020$, $+0.218$] & Partial & Exp.~13, it.~5 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}
\vspace{-0.5em}

\section{What failed}

\textbf{Lineage naturalisation ($A^*_h$):} failed all clauses; within-field sign flips (iteration~1).
\textbf{Gateway retention:} the $+0.103$ AUC was a false positive; full-panel $\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$ (iteration~2).
\textbf{Co-author groups:} untested (REPL stall); not refuted.
\textbf{Within-concept closure:} NOT SUPPORTED; OPEN had opposite-signed effects (iteration~5).
\textbf{Trajectory typology:} no classification passed the naming rule; breadth is a continuum.
\textbf{O1 gateway gains:} all 8 were label-coverage artefacts.

\section{Open questions}

\begin{itemize}[nosep,leftmargin=1.5em]
    \item OPEN$_{\text{home}}$ is modest (PSP $+0.069$ pooled), no forecasting gain over B5. Split-half reliability 0.49.
    \item Temporal-turnover untested (V2 excess reliability $<0.05$), not settled.
    \item Volume-matched retained-field relatedness is null; $d_0$ reverses under an alternative backbone.
    \item Life \& Environment weakness unexplained. Frame~N small ($n = 448$, power 0.47).
    \item About half of M0\_density\_end and D\_vol\_end is pre-onset footprint.
\end{itemize}

\smallskip
The full report is 26 pages.

\end{document}

The association behaves like a static topical-dispersion property of the home neighbourhood; temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted (V2 excess split-half reliability below 0.05). The practical forecasting gain over the five-feature popularity baseline is near zero ($+0.002$ [$-0.003$, $+0.008$]).\n\nA second confirmed result: on the Experiment~7 independent frame (11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events; iteration~3), a conditional logit shows that concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them: $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355]. The pre-registered verdict is FRONTIER $=$ PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null and the coefficient reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity.\n\n\\section{Goal}\n\nThe run investigated whether the early structure of a scientific concept's topic co-occurrence network predicts its later cross-field breadth, beyond simple measures of volume and reach. Using the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (476 million works), it identified 12,499 concepts, tracked 27,393 adoption episodes across 26 fields, and screened 53 early network indicators from six families against a five-feature popularity baseline on held-out field groups. A second question asked whether concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them.\n\n\\section{What was tried}\n\n\\textbf{Iteration 1} raced five rival spread signals (lineage naturalisation, co-author groups, co-occurrence diversity, selectivity, gateway landing) on a 48-concept DEV panel. None survived the pre-registered rule. Two artifacts failed (REPL stalls). The gateway-retention lead ($+0.103$ AUC on 80 episodes) was the only positive signal.\n\n\\textbf{Iteration 2} built the full 12,499-concept frame from a zero-credit OpenAlex S3 scan, tested gateway retention on the full panel (disconfirmed: $\\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$), and confirmed retained-field relatedness for field entry ($d_0 = 0.30$).\n\n\\textbf{Iteration 3} ran the definitive held-out indicator screen (53 indicators; 7 confirmed for breadth), defined the OPEN index (six ego-network components), and tested retained-field relatedness on an independent 11,841-concept frame ($d_0 = 0.322$).\n\n\\textbf{Iteration 4} confirmed OPEN on a fresh 2015--2017 cohort (marginal: OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ PSP $+0.091$ at R2, DL pool CI includes zero), decomposed breadth into exploration (73\\%) and retention (27\\%), and tested openness robustness (specification curve 99.7\\% positive).\n\n\\textbf{Iteration 5} confirmed the signal on vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts (Frame~N: $+0.117$ at R3), rebuilt the Cheng consistency--breadth reversal, completed the within-concept closure test (not supported), decomposed which partners carry the signal, and showed the association is topical non-redundancy, not temporal turnover.\n\n\\section{Key results}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.15}\n\\begin{tabularx}{\\textwidth}{p{3.8cm}p{3.5cm}cX}\n\\toprule\nFinding & Effect & Grade & Source \\\\\n\\midrule\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ predicts breadth (non-selection pool) & PSP $+0.069$ [$+0.038$, $+0.100$]; $I^2\\!=\\!0$ & Lead & Eval.~4, iter.~5 \\\\\nOPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ on confirmatory cohort & PSP $+0.091$ [$+0.013$, $+0.171$] at R2 & Marginal & Exp.~10, iter.~4 \\\\\nRetained-field relatedness $\\to$ entry & $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] & Partial & Exp.~7, iter.~3 \\\\\n7/10 indicators confirmed & DL pooled, Holm $p < 0.05$ & Confirmed & Exp.~8, iter.~3 \\\\\nConsistency $\\to$ volume & $+53\\%$/SD & Replicated & Exp.~14, iter.~5 \\\\\nConsistency $\\to$ narrower breadth & $-0.079$, 5/5 neg., $I^2\\!=\\!0$ & Replicated & Exp.~14, iter.~5 \\\\\nBreadth decomposition & 73\\% exploration & Supported & Exp.~12, iter.~4 \\\\\nSignal $=$ topical dispersion & V2 excess null ($+0.008$) & Descriptive & Exp.~16, iter.~5 \\\\\nFrame~N confirmation & PSP $+0.117$ [$+0.020$, $+0.218$] & Partial & Exp.~13, iter.~5 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabularx}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\section{What failed}\n\n\\textbf{Lineage naturalisation ($A^*_h$):} failed all pre-registered clauses; within-field sign flips (iteration~1).\n\\textbf{Gateway-field retention:} the $+0.103$ AUC lead was a false positive; on the full panel $\\Delta$AUC $= -0.00001$ (iteration~2).\n\\textbf{Co-author groups} (candidate S): untested (REPL stall); not refuted.\n\\textbf{Within-concept closure:} NOT SUPPORTED; OPEN had opposite-signed effects (iteration~5).\n\\textbf{Trajectory typology:} no discrete classification passed the naming rule; breadth is a continuum.\n\\textbf{O1 gateway gains:} all 8 G-variant uptake gains were label-coverage artefacts.\n\n\\section{Open questions}\n\n\\begin{itemize}\n\\setlength{\\itemsep}{0.2em}\n    \\item The OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ effect is modest (PSP $+0.069$ pooled) with no practical forecasting gain over B5 ($+0.002$ [$-0.003$, $+0.008$] Spearman increment).\n    \\item Split-half reliability of OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$ is 0.49; measurement noise is substantial at typical sample sizes (median approximately 30 home papers in the early window).\n    \\item The temporal-turnover question is untested rather than settled: V2 excess split-half reliability is below 0.05, so the within-concept permutation null cannot distinguish year-to-year churn from static topical dispersion.\n    \\item The volume-matched retained-field relatedness contrast is null; $d_0$ reverses under an alternative backbone (minimum-conditional-probability proximity: $d_0 = -0.021$). Persistence versus sustained volume as a predictor of field entry cannot be separated.\n    \\item Life \\& Environment Sciences show the weakest OPEN signal (PSP $+0.071$ versus $+0.186$ for the other five units pooled); the reason is unexplained (not coverage, not range restriction).\n    \\item Frame~N is small ($n = 448$ with OPEN$_{\\text{home}}$) with pre-unseal power of only 0.47; the persistence-filtered RCA density rival ($D_{\\text{rca,persist},k}$) remains untested.\n    \\item About half of M0\\_density\\_end and D\\_vol\\_end is pre-onset footprint, not purely early network dynamics.\n\\end{itemize}\n\n\\medskip\nThe full report is 26 pages.\n\n\\end{document}\n", "userModified": false}

The claim is that this holds beyond the concept's early popularity and reach, the field's\n      size, its relatedness to the concept's home field and the field's general habit of keeping concepts. Then explain it:\n      show the rescue-and-relay flows the mechanism implies, and derive the empirical diffusion trajectories (RQ2) that separate\n      locally concentrated concepts from broadly integrated ones. Together this is a validated, episode-level network account\n      of emergence. It directly contradicts the principle of relatedness at the field-adoption level and reframes RQ1: the\n      portable signal sits in WHERE a concept lands, not in concept-level structure. It is backed by independent external-recognition\n      ground truth and a related-work comparison drawn from the target journal.\n    rationale: >-\n      Iteration 1 ran a wide screen. All three concept-level candidates failed the pre-registered rule (A*_h -0.006; D_ratio\n      +0.006; G +0.033). One lead came out of it: at the field level, adding the adopting field's gateway centrality to B5\n      raised retention AUC from 0.705 to 0.808 (+0.103, 95% CI [0.034, 0.167]). The gain survives a field-size control, is\n      flat for relatedness-to-home (-0.000), is positive in Engineering, BGM and Medicine, and is absent in CS. The lineage\n      experiment independently showed that cross-field behaviour varies mostly at the concept x field level (tau_cj 0.65 vs\n      tau_c 0.29). So the unit of emergence is the adoption episode, and the lead lives exactly there. The updated hypothesis\n      therefore moves to DEEPEN. That is not the same as shrinking. The lead is small (80 rows, 28 concepts, fixed-prediction\n      CI, no trait control, dev only). Its best outcome is also a stronger claim than the original: a position-based rescue\n      effect that beats the field's standard relatedness model. What would kill it is known and cheap to test: 'gateway fields\n      just keep everything', 'any hub metric works', or 'it is a CS/non-CS artefact'. The strategy spends its slots on (1)\n      the decisive scaled test with every named confound and a sealed held-out run; (2) the mechanism and RQ2 trajectories,\n      which the paper needs whatever H1's size; (3) an immediate zero-cost stress test on the iteration-1 data. That test\n      includes a 4.6x replication on the lineage experiment's 367 field-level units, which carry different (Semantic Scholar)\n      labels. It gives a go/no-go and a power figure within hours. (4) Independent external ground truth (the user's step\n      4), which none of iteration 1 had. (5) The target-journal related-work comparison the user explicitly requires. Every\n      data-building artifact uses the same zero-credit snapshot recipe S1, because the shared OpenAlex credit pool ran dry\n      in iteration 1.\n    expected_outcome: >-\n      After this iteration: (1) A decisive H1 answer on sealed held-out evidence. It gives the pooled delta-AUC of gateway_j\n      over the full covariate set (B5, size, relatedness-to-home, density, field retention propensity, insularity, coverage),\n      with concept-clustered refit CIs, per-group and cohort signs, a random-effects I^2, concept- and field-FE estimates,\n      a rewired-backbone placebo and the boundary test explaining CS. Alongside it comes the head-to-head against the relatedness\n      model and the H3 partial rho. (2) The authoritative S1 frame, episode and outcome tables (>= 400 grounded concepts,\n      >= 4,000 episodes, no source truncation), which iteration 3 builds on. (3) RQ2 results: the H2 next-field-entry test,\n      rescue (re-import) and relay evidence, an empirically derived trajectory taxonomy with stability scores, the gateway-before-take-off\n      ordering test, and 4-6 case-study figures. (4) An early go/no-go on the lead: a 367-unit replication with different\n      labels, the trait-confound and placebo results, the power figure and corrected iteration-1 tables. (5) External-recognition\n      ground truth (MeSH, Wikipedia, Wikidata, dated taxonomies, curated breakthrough lists) keyed by QID. (6) A verified\n      related-work comparison table and reference list from the target journal. Because two data builds follow the same recipe\n      S1, iteration 3 can join them and report agreement, then use the frozen top-10 RQ1 indicator matrix (iteration-1 indicators\n      recomputed on S1, scored once on held-out) plus the O5 outcome for the final paper. INFORMATIVE EITHER WAY: if gateway_j\n      dies under the field retention propensity or field FE, retention is a trait of the adopting field, which contradicts\n      both the relatedness principle and concept-level emergence indicators, and the paper reports that.\n  plans:\n  - id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx1\n    type: experiment\n    title: Do hub fields keep new concepts? So results_reported is true. However, the record still contradicts its own evidence\n      in several places, and it drops results that go against its conclusions. (1) Section 10.3 says H1 is 'DISCONFIRMED by\n      all preregistered criteria'. h1_heldout.json verdict_H1.criteria has lpm_beta_within_gt0_p05 = TRUE: the within-field\n      LPM gives beta 0.068 per SD, p_concept 0.041. (2) The ordering finding is listed under 'Confirmed findings' (Section 16.3), but\n      the artifact's own lead-lag evidence cuts against it.
